note: Family tally: bar 18, line 10, flowchart-or-schematic 4, photo-or-raster-image 1, table-grid 12. The paper is a simulation report, so thirty-three exhibits are chart panels and only four are drawings. Declared gap, not a row: TABLE 3, 'Characteristics of Vehicles' on page 16, is printed and captioned at y=290-300 with a booktabs grid under it holding four rows (Car 1 cell 6 cells/sec 60%, Bus 2 cells 5 cells/sec 30%, Truck 2 cells 3 cells/sec 10%), but the detector returned no region for it - the page's only measured region is the Figure 3 raster below it - so the table is named here instead of being given an invented bbox. The paper therefore prints THIRTEEN tables and twelve are measured. Table 3 prints its caption above its grid like every other table.
rules: Every figure caption in the paper prints BELOW its artwork, including the two on pages 11 and 13 whose art fills the top of the page, while every table caption prints ABOVE its grid, so position never varies inside a family [caption.position]
Nothing is punctuated: the numbering runs bare 'Figure N' and 'Table N' from the first to the last of the forty-five captured exhibits and 'FIGURE' never appears [caption.numbering]

Eighteen of the thirty-three figures print one number and one caption over two side-by-side panels, so the paper shows fifty-one chart panels under thirty-three numbers and every second panel is refused as a fragment rather than counted twice [geometry.panel_count]
The occupancy sweeps, Figures 6 to 15, are flat 2-D line plots in MATLAB default styling: one axes, no gridlines, no in-plot title and a boxed legend inside the upper right corner [geometry.family]

Every comparison figure from 16 to 33 is a grouped bar chart in which light and heavy traffic are two adjacent bars inside ONE panel, never two panels, so the split-to-two-panels decision is made only by the (a)/(b) sub-captions and never by the two traffic regimes [geometry.panel_count]
There is no 3-D, no surface and no perspective anywhere in the paper; the closest thing to a perspective drawing is Figure 4's flat flow chart [geometry.three_d]

The bar panels from 16 to 23 and 27 to 33 print a numeric value above nearly every bar, which lets the reader recover the numbers, while the rule-comparison panels 24 to 26 print none at all [geometry.data_labels]
Eleven of the thirty-three figures are never cited by number in the prose: 3, 6, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 29, 30, 31 and 32 [mention.count]

Five cited figures are named a page or two away from the art - Figure 4 is diagrammed on page 18 and cited on 19, Figure 11 drawn on 26 and cited on 27, Figure 18 drawn on 31 and cited on 32, Figure 21 drawn on 33 and cited on 34, and Figure 24 drawn on 37 but first named only as 'Figure 24(a)' on 39 - so those rows carry negative lead_pages [mention.lead_pages]

The paper's first exhibit number is misapplied: the page-22 sentence that introduces the two time-space diagrams calls them '(Figure 8)', which is the flow-rate-of-each-lane figure printed three pages later, leaving Figure 6 with no named citation at all and giving Figure 8 a lead of three pages [mention.style]

The two symbol tables are the only merged-cell tables in the paper, each carrying a single spanning group row - Constants on page 8, Variables on page 9 - over a second, ordinary header row [table.merged_cells]

Two table constructions are in use: the six evaluated-rule and sensitivity tables on pages 40 to 44 keep one internal vertical rule between the stub and the first data column, while the four sensitivity tables on pages 45 and 46 carry horizontal rules only [table.rule_style]
No table is shaded, no table is continued across a page break, and no table prints a note row; every grid is portrait and full measure [table.zebra]

Cells wrap rather than abbreviate: rule names, 'sharp breaking frequency' and 'std. deviation of speed' all break over two lines, and the percent stub of the sensitivity tables prints no header at all [table.header_rows]
